title: Joseph Harris and the neighborhood of musicians
summary: He names the snare player in the kazoo band and the old musicians who lived in his neighborhood.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I thought about a name of Joseph Harris.
And he never did film? No.

He was a nice snap drum player too. He never did take any lesson or nothing. This guy around the street playing like I did. Maybe nobody got interested in the fall like they did me. Probably that's why they didn't get it. But he never played, you know.
I guess you were living there Willie Parker or something. I was. Has he been there where he is now for years?

Yeah, well he was staying right around the corner. Two doors from this old professor. I was telling you, Professor Charlie Lee, he was staying two doors from him. And he stood there, I'd say about 35 years in that one house. And after he moved from there, he moved where he's staying at now. It's in Fuller Street. That's the only two places I've ever learned this day.
And he was staying at the same time. So it was partly a matter of just being lucky to live near somebody who was a nice guy and played music and helped him.

Well all those old musicians that I called was right around the same neighborhood. Trish Kelly, Willie Parker, Kit Howard, Professor Shalini, Miss Albert Snaya. He was staying at the same neighborhood. He was staying at the same neighborhood. Let me see. Well Rene didn't stay around there, but he used to be around that neighborhood quite often. But all those guys right around that same neighborhood. Followed by the neighborhood. Now Guy, yeah, he used to, I was a banjo player. He used to play banjo and trombone. Well he used to run from my, from my mother then. He was staying with us one time. In fact, he gave me a baritone. He used to play baritone too. He gave me a baritone on one time. I didn't know somebody fooled me out of being a kid and I was quite a way. I didn't know the value of it. But I wasn't interested in no horn. I wasn't interested in them drums. I liked the drums. If it had been a set of drums together, I don't guess they would have fooled me out of them. No, I didn't.
